solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: OK then, start off each spring

indicators.note: to take the start off a word is to drop its opening letter

parts.note: each and every are synonyms; its first letter goes
a spring is a source of water, like a well

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, then tells the team to set off every spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but it is a water source; 'start off' trims EVERY to VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Said grudgingly, the phrase is an interjection of agreement, a synonym for a reluctant 'all right, then'.

clue.text: Very old driving licence possibly no longer valid

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a driving licence is one example of identification; 'possibly' marks the example

explanation.surface: An ancient driving licence has probably expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' reads as one description of the licence, but each word gives its own single-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract or ticket that is void has lost its legal force, a direct synonym for being invalid.

clue.text: Some threadbare trousers back in fashion?

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run lying inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Worn-out trousers might be fashionable again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' tempts a solver to read the letters right to left, but they run forwards across the two words; the question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles imitate those of an earlier era, so they are old looks brought into vogue again.

clue.text: Confusion with rowers and boxer

parts.note: a welter is a confused jumble
W is a common abbreviation for with
a racing crew of eight rowers is called an eight

explanation.surface: A chaotic scene involving a rowing crew and a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowers' suggests a mixed group of people, but it means a racing boat's crew, called an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a weight division in boxing, so a fighter in that class is named after it: an example of a boxer.

clue.text: Bible reading given by the French boy

parts.note: les is the French plural 'the'
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A French lad reads a passage of scripture in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' looks like a nationality describing the boy, but it is the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: In church services, a passage of scripture read aloud to the congregation is traditionally called a lesson.

clue.text: Musical work featured in Octopussy

indicators.note: what is featured in something appears inside it, so the letters sit within the word

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the film title

explanation.surface: A piece of music appears in the James Bond film Octopussy.
explanation.walkthrough: Octopussy is a 1983 James Bond film; the surface suggests its soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers number their compositions as opus numbers, so the Latin word for 'work' names a piece of music.

clue.text: Short bio for item in a folder

parts.note: to be pro something is to be for it
a folder holds files

explanation.surface: A brief biography is kept as a document in someone's folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a mere link word but supplies the Latin-derived prefix meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a concise written portrait of a person, as in a newspaper or dating site, the same as a brief biography.

clue.text: Band occasionally breaking into calm, romantic tune

indicators.note: breaking into a place means entering it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: serene means calm

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A group of musicians now and then interrupts a gentle love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, fitting the romantic tune, but it only supplies two of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song traditionally sung or played beneath a sweetheart's window in the evening.

clue.text: Hugely exciting proceedings in a court crowded with people

parts.note: a legal action is a set of proceedings in court
a packed room is crowded

explanation.surface: A thrilling trial plays out in a courtroom full of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one courtroom drama, but splits into a legal term and a word for crowded.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or story full of thrilling events and incident is described this way, meaning very lively and exciting.

clue.text: Heads of inquiry never permitted to return useful info

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: the initials of the two words

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: let means permitted

explanation.surface: Leaders of an investigation were never allowed to hand back helpful information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' suggests people in charge of the inquiry, but it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intel is informal shorthand for intelligence, meaning gathered information, especially military or police knowledge.

clue.text: Help fool coming out of trap?

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so whatever comes out of it is spoken

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A dupe is being rescued from a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' suggests a snare that a fool is caught in, but it is slang for mouth, so the word is spoken. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is an old-fashioned word for assistance or relief given in time of hardship.

clue.text: The 90th Parallel North is one good place from which to start

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: latitude 90 degrees north is where the North Pole sits

definitions.text: good place from which to start
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the front spot on a motor-racing grid

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: 90 degrees north is a single point, the location of a pole, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the fastest qualifier starts at the front of the grid, the most advantageous starting slot.

clue.text: Teacher's sexy yearbook photo?

parts.note: a head teacher is the head, and the possessive adds S
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: A teacher's glamorous picture in the school yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the head is the headteacher, the principal of a school; the question mark marks the yearbook picture as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A headshot is a portrait photograph of face and shoulders, exactly the kind printed beside each name in a yearbook.

clue.text: Barges are ultimately slow moving around middle of harbour

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of their order
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it

parts.note: the four letters rearranged

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the fourth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: Barges eventually move slowly around the inner harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barges' looks like a noun for boats, matching the harbour, but it is a verb meaning pushes roughly through.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to shove one's way forward with the arms, just as someone barges through a crowd.

clue.text: Second-rate train travelling across one country

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move, out of their printed order

parts.note: B grade is second rate, after A

indicators.note: to lie across something is to straddle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A poor-quality train service crosses a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train travelling' reads as a rail journey, but 'travelling' scrambles the word, and 'one' is the Roman numeral placed within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain, shortened in everyday use, is a nation of the United Kingdom's island, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Mean video games company rejecting outsiders

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its outer letters, and rejecting them throws them away

parts.note: Nintendo is the Japanese maker of the Switch and Mario games

explanation.surface: A stingy gaming firm turns away people from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for stingy, but it is the verb meaning to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan or have the purpose of doing it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Business schedule information penned by a district attorney

indicators.note: what is penned is shut in as if in a pen, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: taken as written
gen is British slang for information
DA is the standard abbreviation for district attorney

explanation.surface: A prosecutor writes down details of the day's legal business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed, as in a sheep pen. Gen is British slang for the facts or the lowdown.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be discussed at a meeting, so it is a programme for business.

clue.text: Form of sports practice compelling misplaced anger

definitions.note: the answer is the place where this practice happens

indicators.note: letters that are misplaced have been put in the wrong positions

parts.note: a driving force is a compelling one
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete's training session is fuelled by frustration aimed at the wrong target.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it names a facility, not an activity, where golfers hit balls to practise their long shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers go to this open area to practise tee shots, so it stands for a kind of sporting training.

clue.text: Manager almost makes mistake

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: British slang for a boss or football manager

explanation.surface: A boss nearly gets something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a gaffer is a boss, often a football team's manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing slip, a direct synonym for an error.

clue.text: Something folded that always comes open at the front

definitions.text: Something folded that always comes open at the front

indicators.note: what is at the front of each word is its initial letter

parts.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A folded item whose front edge never closes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while its last words also supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla shell is folded around a filling and left open along one side, exactly as described.

clue.text: Uncivilised male withdrawing south from capital

indicators.note: withdrawing something takes it away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
the capital of Greece loses S, the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A boorish man retreats south from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing south' reads as travel, but it removes the S from the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, once meaning non-believer, is used loosely as an adjective for barbaric or lacking culture.

clue.text: Part of pack of takeaway meatballs

indicators.note: only a part of the following letters is used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the letters span the three words

explanation.surface: Some of the meatballs from a takeaway carton.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run straight through the end of one word, all of the next, and the start of the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Kofta are spiced minced-meat balls or patties from South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking, and the word serves as a plural.

clue.text: Bite from flipping insect!

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about being stung by a wretched bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bite' suggests an insect sting, but it means a sharp flavour; 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, piquant taste, and a sauce with bite has that pungent quality.

clue.text: Agonised about location in California

indicators.note: about can mean in a different order, as letters turned round and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fretted over a spot on the West Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it rearranges the letters of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major city on the Pacific coast near the Mexican border, so it is an example of a place in that state.
